NOTE 2 is non-normative. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Same two grounds as GR14, re-measured for the binary64 half. The format claim holds for an item declared at its own level: FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH 8; MOVE 16777217 keeps 16777217 where the FLOAT-BINARY-32 sibling in the same program rounds to 16777216; MOVE 9007199254740993 stores 9007199254740992 - the binary64 rounding of 2**53+1, which is the sharpest single discriminator of binary64 there is and which the adjudicator did not run; MOVE 1.0E-320 survives as a binary64 subnormal and MOVE 1.0E308 is held exactly. GROUND 1 - the inherited declaration shape. SS13.18.60.4 GR1 (cite-checked) makes a group-level USAGE clause apply to each elementary item in the group, and `01 GT USAGE FLOAT-BINARY-64.  05 AT2.` compiles with NO diagnostic, exit 0, and gives AT2 FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH 0 - the phrase specified nothing, where the rule says it 'specifies that the data item IS a floating-point data item in 64-bit basic binary interchange format'. In the SAME program the SS13.18.60.3 SR2 form `05 AL USAGE FLOAT-BINARY-64.` under the same group gives 8, and `01 GI USAGE INDEX.  05 AI.` gives 8, so the group clause is accepted and the picture-less resolution machinery exists but was built for USAGE INDEX only; a MOVE into such an item crashes the compiler with an unhandled NullReferenceException rather than diagnosing it. The same SS13.16.3 SR8 caveat as GR14 applies and is stated there. GROUND 2 - the cited test does not pin this rule's distinguishing branch: conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/float_binary is spec-derived but uses only 10.5, 100.25 and their integer products, every one of which is exactly representable in binary32 as well, so it separates binary64 from binary32 by WIDTH alone, never by format. NOTE FOR THE REGISTRAR: the inheritance defect is ONE root cause shared with my GR12, GR13, GR14 and GR21 verdicts - one fix closes all five. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/PictureAnalyzer.cs#PictureAnalyzer.ParseUsage; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.ClrType; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.ByteForm; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolFloat.cs || CLOSED 2026-09-09 by kb/Work PB495 (landed). The REFUTED paragraph above names the ONE root it shares with GR13, GR14, GR15 and GR21 -- "picture-less group-usage inheritance implemented for INDEX only" -- and says in terms that one fix closes all five. That fix is landed: 13.18.60.4 GR1 is now implemented as an EQUIVALENCE rather than as a special case, over ONE derivation of an elementary item's effective usage (its own USAGE clause, else the nearest enclosing one) feeding the group-header shed, the leaf's representation and every 13.18.60.3 screen through the same code the written-clause path runs. So `01 GB USAGE BINARY-SHORT. 05 AB.` is a 2-byte binary item and `01 GF USAGE FLOAT-LONG. 05 AL.` an 8-byte floating-point one, not the ZERO-LENGTH cells measured above, and the MOVE that crashed the compiler with an unhandled NullReferenceException in MoveEmitter.ConvertSource runs. RE-MEASURED, both spellings, whole matrix: a (usage x picture x arm) sweep of 138 cells found 108 DIFFERING on the pre-fix tree 39479e19 and 0 differing after, and the equivalence is now a drift theory over the whole Usage enum rather than a set of cases. The spec-derived witnesses are the two new goldens: conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb495_group_usage_applies_to_each_leaf prints W=1 2 4 8 4 8 8 (binary-char/-short/-long/-double, float-short, float-long, index) with GRP=4 for a two-leaf BINARY-SHORT group and CTL=2 for the written-clause control, and conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb495_group_usage_standard_float prints W=4 8 2 2 with F=16777216 16777217 -- 2**24+1 rounded by binary32 and held exactly by binary64, the sharpest single discriminator between the two interchange formats -- and N=-32768 65535, which is GR21 sentence 2's SIGNED/UNSIGNED length identity together with the UNSIGNED phrase reaching the leaf from the group entry. Everything the REFUTED paragraph credits as already holding is unchanged.
